laws.rule: Hamburg charges a culture and tourism tax (Kultur- und Tourismustaxe) on every paid overnight stay, graded by the net room price per person; breakfast and other extras are not taxed. The host owes it and may pass it on to guests.
laws.heading: Hamburgisches Kultur- und Tourismustaxengesetz
Hamburgisches Passivraucherschutzgesetz (HmbPSchG) section 2 and section 5
laws.rule: Hamburg bans smoking tobacco and cannabis products, including e-cigarettes, heated tobacco and vaporisers, in enclosed rooms of public offices and courts, hospitals, care homes, schools, universities, sports halls, culture venues, bars and restaurants (including discos), food shops, indoor shopping centres, betting shops and gaming halls (section 2(1) and (2)). A smoker can get a free warning or a fine of EUR 20 to 400 (about A$32 to A$636); an operator who skips the sign or does not act can be fined EUR 50 to 1,000 (about A$79 to A$1,589) (section 5(2)). AUD at A$1 = EUR 0.6293 (RBA, 30 Oct 2026).
laws.penalty_signal: Smoker EUR 20 to 400; operator EUR 50 to 1,000.

laws.heading: Landeswaldgesetz (Hamburg) section 9, section 10 and section 15
laws.rule: In Hamburg's forests, camping with a tent and parking vehicles or caravans need the owner's special permission (section 9(3)). A fire or open light outside a marked fireplace in the forest needs a permit (section 10(1)). From 1 March to 31 October smoking in the forest is banned outside buildings and official vehicles; the rest of the year smoking is allowed only on roads and paths (section 10(3)). Throwing away burning things or glass is banned (section 10(4)). Fines are mostly up to EUR 2,500 (about A$3,973), up to EUR 10,000 (about A$15,890) in especially serious cases, and up to EUR 25,000 (about A$39,725) for the offences in section 15(1) Nr. 1 and 4a (section 15(2)). AUD at A$1 = EUR 0.6293 (RBA, 30 Oct 2026).
laws.penalty_signal: Up to EUR 2,500; up to EUR 25,000 for the gravest listed offences.
